column4: Visit note | 2025-02-19 12:30 PM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Nurul Ahmed, 73, male. Mr. Ahmed returns for review and reports ongoing dizziness whenever he looks up, along with brief spinning sensations when he turns in bed, which trigger mild nausea. He is a shopkeeper and mentions these spells began after bumping his head on a rickshaw hood in Rajshahi. He has no other major health conditions. He denies double vision, weakness, or hearing loss. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 116/80 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 91 kg. Cranial nerves are intact. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-22 04:30 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Dilruba Matubbar, 67, female. Mrs. Matubbar comes in for her first visit complaining of dizziness whenever she looks up and brief spinning episodes when turning in bed. She works as a madrasa teacher and states her symptoms started after a long bus ride to Khilgaon. She has a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any limb weakness, numbness, or fainting. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 129/83 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 49 kg. Gait is steady with caution. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
